21784-the-goblins-christmas.title: The Goblins' Christmas
21784-the-goblins-christmas.creator: Unknown
21784-the-goblins-christmas.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. laughed  With a shrill and sneering jibe;  Her soul grew fat to see them chaffed,  This mad and elfish tribe. The big black caldron boiled so high  With food for these queer mites,  That it lit the world throughout the sky,  And down came all the Sprites.

arxiv-2012-15692.title: NeuralMagicEye: Learning to See and Understand the Scene Behind an Autostereogram
arxiv-2012-15692.creator: Zhengxia Zou, Tianyang Shi, Yi Yuan, Zhenwei Shi
arxiv-2012-15692.description: Abstract An autostereogram, a.k.a. magic eye image, is a single-image stereogram that can create visual illusions of 3D scenes from 2D textures. This paper studies an interesting question that whether a deep CNN can be trained to recover the depth behind an autostereogram and understand its content.

arxiv-2101-01678.title: Link invariants from L 2 L^{2} -Burau maps of braids
arxiv-2101-01678.creator: Fathi Ben Aribi
arxiv-2101-01678.description: Abstract . A previous work of A. Conway and the author introduced L 2 L^{2} -Burau maps of braids, which are generalizations of the Burau representation whose coefficients live in a more general group ring than the one of Laurent polynomials.

arxiv-2102-00959.title: Bounds on abundance of primordial black hole and dark matter from EDGES 21-cm signal
arxiv-2102-00959.creator: Ashadul Halder, Shibaji Banerjee
arxiv-2102-00959.description: Abstract The redshifted 21cm radio signal has emerged as an important probe for investigating the dynamics of the dark age Universe (recombination to reionization). In the current analysis, we explore the combined effect of primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation and the baryon-dark matter (DM) interaction in the 21cm scenario.

arxiv-2110-08381.title: On The Ingredients of an Effective Zero-shot Semantic Parser
arxiv-2110-08381.creator: Pengcheng Yin, John Wieting, Avi Sil, Graham Neubig
arxiv-2110-08381.description: Abstract Semantic parsers map natural language utterances into meaning representations ( e.g. programs). Such models are typically bottlenecked by the paucity of training data due to the required laborious annotation efforts. Recent studies have performed zero-shot learning by synthesizing training examples of canonical utterances and programs from a grammar, and further paraphrasing these utterances to improve linguistic diversity.

arxiv-2309-05531.title: Inverse probability of treatment weighting with generalized linear outcome models for doubly robust estimation
arxiv-2309-05531.creator: Erin E Gabriel*, Michael C Sachs, Torben Martinussen, Ingeborg Waernbaum, Els Goetghebeur, Stijn Vansteelandt, Arvid Sjölander
arxiv-2309-05531.description: Abstract There are now many options for doubly robust estimation; however, there is a concerning trend in the applied literature to believe that the combination of a propensity score and an adjusted outcome model automatically results in a doubly robust estimator and/or to misuse more complex established doubly robust estimators.

arxiv-2411-18964.title: Neural Operators for Predictor Feedback Control of Nonlinear Delay Systems
arxiv-2411-18964.creator: Luke Bhan, Peijia Qin, Miroslav Krstic, Yuanyuan Shi
arxiv-2411-18964.description: Abstract Predictor feedback designs are critical for delay-compensating controllers in nonlinear systems. However, these designs are limited in practical applications as predictors cannot be directly implemented, but require numerical approximation schemes, which become computationally prohibitive when system dynamics are expensive to compute.

arxiv-2412-14985.title: Exploration of the Dynamics of Buy and Sale of Social Media Accounts
arxiv-2412-14985.creator: Mario Beluri, Bhupendra Acharya, Soheil Khodayari, Giada Stivala, Giancarlo Pellegrino, Thorsten Holz
arxiv-2412-14985.description: Abstract Abstract There has been a rise in online platforms facilitating the buying and selling of social media accounts. While the trade of social media profiles is not inherently illegal, social media platforms view such transactions as violations of their policies. They often take action against accounts involved in the misuse of platforms for financial gain.

arxiv-2502-07424.title: RomanLens: The Role of Latent Romanization in Multilinguality in LLMs
arxiv-2502-07424.creator: Alan Saji, Jaavid Aktar Husain, Thanmay Jayakumar, Raj Dabre, Anoop Kunchukuttan, Ratish Puduppully
arxiv-2502-07424.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong multilingual performance despite being predominantly trained on English-centric corpora. This raises a fundamental question: How do LLMs achieve such multilingual capabilities? Focusing on languages written in non-Roman scripts, we investigate the role of Romanization—the representation of non-Roman scripts using Roman characters—as a potential bridge in multilingual processing.

arxiv-2508-04225.title: Symmetric Behavior Regularization via Taylor Expansion of Symmetry
arxiv-2508-04225.creator: Lingwei Zhu, Zheng Chen, Han Wang, Yukie Nagai
arxiv-2508-04225.description: Abstract This paper introduces symmetric divergences to behavior regularization policy optimization (BRPO) to establish a novel offline RL framework. Existing methods focus on asymmetric divergences such as KL to obtain analytic regularized policies and a practical minimization objective. We show that symmetric divergences do not permit an analytic policy as regularization and can incur numerical issues as loss.

arxiv-2601-16563.title: Process-Tensor Tomography of SGD: Measuring Non-Markovian Memory via Back-Flow of Distinguishability Thanks: Citation ( to appear in ) : Vasileios Sevetlidis, and George Pavlidis. Process-Tensor Tomography of SGD: Measuring Non-Markovian Memory via Back-Flow of Distinguishability. Proceedings of The
arxiv-2601-16563.creator: Vasileios Sevetlidis*, George Pavlidis
arxiv-2601-16563.description: Abstract This work proposes neural training as a process tensor : a multi-time map that takes a sequence of controllable instruments (batch choices, augmentations, optimizer micro-steps) and returns an observable of the trained model. Building on this operational lens, we introduce a simple, model-agnostic witness of training memory based on back-flow of distinguishability .

arxiv-2602-10302.title: Totally decomposable algebras with involution and R R -triviality
arxiv-2602-10302.creator: M. Archita, Karim Johannes Becher
arxiv-2602-10302.description: Abstract . We show that the group of proper projective similitudes of a totally decomposable algebra with involution of the first kind over a field of characteristic different from 2 2 is R R -trivial. Keywords: Classical adjoint algebraic group, stably rational, R R -equivalence, quadratic form, hyperbolic, Pfister form Classification (MSC 2020): 11E04, 11E57, 11E81, 14E08, 20G15 1.

pmc-10643234.title: Triglyceride Glucose Index is Strongly Associated with a Fragility Fracture in Postmenopausal Elderly Females with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Combined with Osteoporosis: A 6-Year Follow-Up Study
pmc-10643234.creator: Jiangmei Pan, Xiuxian Huang, Qiu Wang, Jingxia Sun, Zhenwei Zhai, Jiacheng Mo, Jianhao Huang, Wensheng Lu
pmc-10643234.description: PurposeThe triglyceride glucose (TyG) index serves as an indicator of insulin resistance (IR), which is also associated with bone metabolism. However, research on the relationship between the TyG index and a fragility fracture in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) or osteoporosis (OP) remains sparse.

pmc-11458974.title: Influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis via sensitive testing methods in clinical application
pmc-11458974.creator: Le Zhang, Chunwen Li, ShaSha Shao, Zhaowei Zhang, Di Chen
pmc-11458974.description: The identification of influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2 has garnered increasing attention due of their longstanding global menace to human life and health. The point-of-care test is a potential approach for identifying influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2 in clinical settings, leading to timely discovery, documentation, and treatment.

pmc-11686654.title: Risk Factors for Infectious and Soft Tissue Complications in Ankle Fracture Dislocations
pmc-11686654.creator: Chirag Soni, Adam Zhuang, Kylee Faith Darden, Malynda Wynn, Alex Benedick, Jan P Szatkowski, Yohan Jang, Roman Natoli, Luke A Lopas
pmc-11686654.description: Category:Trauma; AnkleIntroduction/Purpose:Ankle fracture-dislocations (AFD) are violent injuries with reported worse prognosis compared to their non-dislocated counterparts. There is limited literature describing the demographic characteristics and risk factors for complications for these injuries. This study analyzed risk factors for deep surgical site infection and wound complications in AFDs.

pmc-12417323.title: Extrachromosomal Circular DNA as a Cancer Biomarker: From Diagnosis to Treatment
pmc-12417323.creator: Hexin Li, Jiahui Cai, Gang Zhao, Lihui Zou
pmc-12417323.description: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an emerging class of genetic material that exists outside of the chromosomal genome. These circular DNA molecules are gaining increasing attention as important biomarkers in various cancers because of their roles in gene amplification, genetic heterogeneity, and drug resistance.

pmc-12662053.title: Genomic Signatures of Selection Across Climate Gradients and a Geographic Mosaic of Coevolution in an Ant Social Parasite–Host System
pmc-12662053.creator: Maide Nesibe Macit, Erwann Collin, Maria Esther Nieto-Blazquez, Marion Kever, Maria Litto, Esther Jaitner, Markus Pfenninger, Barbara Feldmeyer, Susanne Foitzik, Aya Takahashi
pmc-12662053.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Coevolutionary dynamics in host–parasite systems are shaped by reciprocal selection and environmental context. When hosts and parasites share ancestry and ecological overlap, selection can act on similar traits, but population structure and geography may generate adaptive mosaics. Here, we present the first study to investigate genome-wide signatures of selection in response to a broad climatic gradient and a geographic mosaic of coevolution between a social parasite and its host.

pmc-12667375.title: Personalized neural responses to self and filial reward: Functional and structural responses to motivational cues
pmc-12667375.creator: Siti Mariam Roslan, Siti Hajar Zabri, Nur Ayunie Ayob, Aini Ismafairus Abd Hamid, Nur Hartini Mohd Taib, Rahimah Zakaria, Sofina Tamam, Hazim Omar, Alwani Liyana Ahmad, Wan Mohd Zahiruddin Wan Mohammad, Aleya Aziz Marzuki, Asma Hayati Ahmad
pmc-12667375.description: Understanding how individuals interact with reward-related cues in their environment provides insight into the neural mechanisms underlying motivation and personalized behavior. While monetary rewards for self are well studied, the neural basis of socially relevant rewards—such as filial reward—remains less understood.

pmc-13300015.title: Leadless pacemakers in patients with active haematological cancer: procedural details and long-term clinical outcomes
pmc-13300015.creator: M Farkowski, I Zastawna, R Supryn, P Rusztyn, B Lech, K Gajos, I Hus, R Gil
pmc-13300015.description: Background/Introductionleadless pacemakers (LPR) are primarily indicated for patients with bradyarrhythmia and high risk of infection from transvenous pacemaker.(1) Patients with haematological malignancies may be at a risk of device-related infection due to underlying disease and treatment; however available evidence is limited to case-studies.

pmc-13517310.title: Joint Quality–Reliability Analysis of IRS-Assisted Communications in Presence of Inverse Power Lomax Fading Channel
pmc-13517310.creator: Aleksey S. Gvozdarev, Roman Yu. Manakhov
pmc-13517310.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this work, we study the joint performance of the quality and reliability in terms of quality–reliability (JQR) performance of an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted wireless communication system under severe multipath fading and shadowing.

pmc-13608856.title: Persistent Non-albicans Predominance, High Mortality, and Azole-Non-Susceptible Candida tropicalis: A 15-Year Pediatric Invasive Candidiasis Cohort in Southern Thailand
pmc-13608856.creator: Puttichart Khantee, Kochakorn Pinichkijpaisal, Mingkwan Yingkajorn, Therdpong Thongseiratch, Kamolwish Laoprasopwattana
pmc-13608856.description: Invasive candidiasis (IC) causes substantial mortality in critically ill children, yet pediatric data from Southeast Asia remain limited. We retrospectively studied 117 children aged ≤ 18 years with proven IC at a Thai tertiary center (2009–2023). Thirty-day mortality was 25.6%, rising to 47.1% in neonates; death occurred a median of 5.5 days after diagnosis.

uslaw-usc-t22-s2672b.title: 22 U.S.C. § 2672b — Compensation of Alternate United States Commissioners; travel expenses and other allowances
uslaw-usc-t22-s2672b.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s2672b.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 38 (Department Of State). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Alternate United States Commissioners shall receive no compensation for their services. They may be paid travel expenses and per diem in lieu of subsistence at the rates authorized by section 5703 of title 5 when engaged in the performance of their duties.

uslaw-usc-t43-s617n.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s617n.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 12A (Boulder Canyon Project); Subchapter I (Boulder Canyon Project Act). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
